title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): S is an integral scheme of finite type over Z, dominant over Spec Z, with generic point y. X is smooth of finite type over S. E is a locally free O_X-module with an integrable (flat) connection relative to S. The connection on E_y over X_y is called 'of level zero' or 'integrable' if it becomes trivial (as a connection) on some finite étale surjective cover of X_y. Over C this means the transcendental monodromy representation of pi_1 factors through a finite group. A variant replaces E by a G_X-torsor with flat connection, for any S-group scheme G of finite type.

This page:
(1) Easy direction. If E_y is integrable, there is an open neighbourhood U of y in S such that for every s in U of characteristic p>0, the p-curvature of (E_s, nabla) on X_s/s vanishes. Equivalently, E_s is 'integrable' in the char-p sense: it is spanned by horizontal sections, by Cartier descent. Grothendieck remarks that it is equivalent to impose this only at closed points of U.
(2) The question: is the converse true? This is the p-curvature conjecture, now called the Grothendieck–Katz conjecture.
(3) Rank one analysis. E_y integrable means E comes from a Kummer (mu_n) torsor: the connection is induced by a horizontal trivialisation of E^{⊗n} for some n≥1. The question splits in two.
  (a) If p-curvature vanishes at all closed points s of characteristic p>0, is the class of E_y in Pic(X_y) torsion?
  (b) If so, after a Kummer cover one reduces to E ≅ O_X as a module, so nabla = d + omega with omega a closed relative 1-form. The question becomes: if each omega_s is locally logarithmic (locally df/f), is some integer multiple n·omega_y globally logarithmic? The marginal note records the char-p criterion: by Cartier's theorem, a closed form omega_s is locally logarithmic iff C̃(omega_s) = omega_s. This is equivalent to vanishing p-curvature of d+omega.
(4) The next page continues with commutative algebraic groups: affine/unipotent cases are 'trivial' via Chevalley's theorem, reducing to extensions of an abelian variety by a torus. This is the generalised-Jacobian / commutative-group approach to the rank-one case.
errors: Labelling slip: the reduction step is written 'b) Si la réponse est affirmative, on est ramené dans b) ...' and then a second 'b)' states the 1-form question. The first should be an unlabelled transition.

Reducing to E ≅ O_X uses a finite étale (Kummer) cover X'_y → X_y trivialising the torsion line bundle. Question (b) must then be posed on the cover, possibly after shrinking S. This is harmless but left implicit.

In (b), 'a multiple of omega is a dlog' should be read as omega_y = (1/n) df/f for some rational function f, i.e. n·omega_y = dlog f. The conclusion then also needs passing back from the cover. These are minor imprecisions, not real errors.

ideas.what: Integrable (finite-monodromy) connection implies vanishing p-curvature for almost all p, checkable at closed points
ideas.modern_name: easy direction of the Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (folklore); written up by N. Katz (1970, 1972)
ideas.where_published: Katz, 'Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem' (Publ. IHES 1970) and 'Algebraic solutions of differential equations' (Invent. Math. 1972)

ideas.what: Converse question: p-curvature zero for almost all p implies finite monodromy; also posed for G-torsors with flat connection
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (late 1960s), publicised by Katz; torsor variants discussed by André and others
ideas.where_published: Katz 1972; André, 'Sur la conjecture des p-courbures de Grothendieck–Katz et un problème de Dwork' (2004); Bost (2001)

ideas.what: Rank-one splitting: (a) torsion of the class in Pic, (b) closed 1-form with C̃ω_s=ω_s for almost all s implies a multiple of ω is dlog
ideas.modern_name: rank-one case of Grothendieck–Katz via Cartier operator / generalised Jacobians
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz; Chudnovsky–Chudnovsky (curves); proved in general via Bost / André (solvable monodromy)
ideas.where_published: Katz 1972; D.V. & G.V. Chudnovsky (1985); Bost, Publ. IHES 93 (2001); André 2004

ideas.what: Closed form locally logarithmic iff fixed by the Cartier operator; equivalently p-curvature of d+ω vanishes
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Cartier (1957); Katz for the p-curvature formulation
ideas.where_published: Cartier, 'Questions de rationalité des diviseurs en géométrie algébrique' (1958); Katz 1970

missed.claim: This page is a primary-source formulation of the p-curvature conjecture in Grothendieck's own hand. It includes the G-torsor generalisation and an explicit reduction of the rank-one case to a Pic-torsion question plus a Cartier-operator/dlog question. The record attributes the conjecture to Grothendieck only via Katz's reports; this page documents his own formulation and first reduction steps.
missed.quote: Question La réciproque est-elle vraie? ... a) ... est-il vrai que l'image de E dans Pic(X_y) est de torsion? ... b) Si ω est une 1-forme différentielle [fermée] ... sont loc. des différentielles logarithmiques, alors est-il vrai qu'un multiple entier de ω_y est une diff. logarithmique?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical attribution and dating: it shows Grothendieck already viewed the rank-one case through Pic-torsion and commutative group extensions (abelian variety by torus, on the next page). This is essentially the route later taken by Chudnovsky, Bost and André. The mathematics itself is known.

deep.surprise_reason: This is Grothendieck's original handwritten statement of the famous Grothendieck–Katz conjecture, with the rank-one decomposition and a G-torsor variant. That is historically valuable, but the content is well known through Katz and the rank-one case is now a theorem (Bost, André).
transcription_corrections: The marginal phrase 'ou encore, intégrables' refers to rewording the p-curvature condition (E_s generated by horizontal sections); it attaches to the bracketed line 'nulle', not a separate clause.
'Kummérien' is struck out, but the torsor in question is a Kummer (mu_n) torsor, as the following text about trivialising E^{⊗n} shows.
The first 'b)' (the 'ramené au cas où E≃O_X' line) is a transition sentence; only the second 'b)' is the actual sub-question.
The marginal note bottom-left reads 'ce qui se vérifie par l'opération de Cartier C̃ω_s = ω_s'.
